overview.caption: Glucose enters the town, gets split in the shed, then powers the mitochondrion's carousel and dam — unless there's no oxygen, and it takes the fermentation detour.

ideas.title: Glycolysis
ideas.core: In the cytoplasm, without oxygen, glucose (6C) is split into two pyruvate (3C), netting 2 ATP and 2 NADH.
ideas.why_shape: It's a single processing step with inputs, a cost, and outputs: a shed on a rail line.
ideas.caption: A six-car glucose train rolls into the splitting shed, pays 2 ATP to get in, and leaves as two three-car pyruvate trains — 4 ATP made, 2 kept.
ideas.hook: Giant red scissors snip the train in half: 6 → 3 + 3.

questions.q: Where in the cell does glycolysis happen?
What molecule goes into glycolysis, and how many carbons does it have?
What comes out of glycolysis?
questions.answer: Two pyruvate, 3 carbons each (plus ATP and NADH).

questions.q: What is the net ATP gain from glycolysis, and why isn't it 4?
questions.answer: 2 ATP: 4 are made but 2 are invested.

questions.q: Does glycolysis need oxygen?

ideas.title: The Krebs cycle
ideas.core: In the mitochondrial matrix, acetyl-CoA joins oxaloacetate to make citrate; each turn releases 2 CO₂ and makes 3 NADH, 1 FADH₂ and 1 ATP. It turns twice per glucose.
ideas.why_shape: It's a loop that ends where it starts (oxaloacetate comes back), so a carousel.
ideas.caption: Acetyl-CoA climbs onto the carousel next to oxaloacetate, making citrate; every lap lets go of two CO₂ balloons and drops three kinds of prizes.
ideas.hook: Grey CO₂ balloons float away from the carousel — that's the CO₂ you breathe out.

questions.q: Where does the Krebs cycle take place?
What molecule enters the Krebs cycle?
Acetyl-CoA combines with what, and what does it form?
What gas is released, and how much per turn?
How many times does the cycle turn per glucose, and what does each turn produce?
questions.answer: Twice; each turn makes 3 NADH, 1 FADH₂ and 1 ATP.

ideas.title: Electron transport chain
ideas.core: On the inner mitochondrial membrane, electrons from NADH and FADH₂ power pumps that push H⁺ out; H⁺ flows back through ATP synthase, making about 26–28 ATP. Oxygen takes the last electrons and forms water.
ideas.why_shape: A gradient that stores energy and releases it through one gate is a dam with a turbine.
ideas.caption: Electrons hop pump to pump, each hop pushing H⁺ up behind the dam; H⁺ rushes back down through the ATP synthase turbine, and oxygen catches the last electrons.
ideas.hook: Oxygen is a goalkeeper at the end of the line — without it, the electrons pile up and the whole chain stops.

questions.q: Where does the electron transport chain happen?
What does the energy from the electrons do?
questions.answer: Pumps H⁺ ions into the space between the membranes.

questions.q: How is ATP made in this stage?
questions.answer: H⁺ flows back through ATP synthase, which spins and makes ATP.

questions.q: What is the final electron acceptor, and what does it form?
About how much ATP does this stage make?
questions.answer: About 26–28 ATP, most of the total.

ideas.title: With or without oxygen
ideas.core: With oxygen, pyruvate goes on to the Krebs cycle and electron transport (about 30–32 ATP in total). Without it, cells ferment: muscles make lactate, yeast make ethanol and CO₂. Fermentation makes no extra ATP but regenerates NAD⁺ so glycolysis can continue.
ideas.why_shape: One molecule, two possible routes decided by one condition: a fork in the road with a signpost.
ideas.caption: The pyruvate car reaches a signpost asking about oxygen: the upper road pays out a pile of ATP, the lower road only recycles NAD⁺ — into burning legs or rising bread.
ideas.hook: A sprinter with burning legs and a loaf of rising bread sit side by side on the 'no oxygen' road.

questions.q: What decides which way pyruvate goes?
About how much ATP does aerobic respiration make per glucose in total?
What do human muscles make without oxygen?
What does yeast make during fermentation?
Why does fermentation happen if it makes no extra ATP?
questions.answer: It regenerates NAD⁺ so glycolysis can keep making 2 ATP.
